questions.prompt: What accounting shift does moving from on-premises servers to the cloud typically represent?
choices: From CapEx (buying hardware up front) to OpEx (paying as you use)
From OpEx to CapEx
From paying for hardware to paying nothing
From per-use billing to a fixed yearly purchase
questions.answer: From CapEx (buying hardware up front) to OpEx (paying as you use)
questions.explanation: Instead of a large up-front hardware purchase, the cloud bills ongoing usage as an operating expense.

questions.prompt: If a customer leaves their cloud database open to the whole internet with no password, the cloud provider is responsible for the resulting breach under the shared responsibility model.
questions.explanation: Security in the cloud, including configuration and access, is the customer's job; the provider secures the underlying cloud.

questions.prompt: Match each cloud deployment model to its description.
pairs: Shared infrastructure run by a provider
Cloud-style operations dedicated to one organization
Using public and private environments together on purpose
questions.explanation: The three models differ in who the infrastructure is shared with and whether you combine environments.

questions.prompt: What is the key difference between containers and virtual machines?
choices: Containers share the host operating system kernel, while each VM runs its own full OS
Containers each include a full guest OS, while VMs share the host kernel
Containers need physical hardware dedicated to them
VMs cannot run on cloud providers
questions.answer: Containers share the host operating system kernel, while each VM runs its own full OS
questions.explanation: Sharing the kernel makes containers lighter and faster to start than VMs, which duplicate a whole OS.

questions.prompt: Which of these describe serverless computing?
choices: It can scale to zero when idle
Billing is by the millisecond of execution
Functions can suffer cold starts
You patch and manage the underlying operating system
You pay for idle servers around the clock
answers: It can scale to zero when idle
Billing is by the millisecond of execution
questions.explanation: Serverless hides the servers, bills only for running time, and trades that for cold-start delay and short-lived execution.

questions.prompt: What is the name for the extra startup delay a serverless function can have when it runs after sitting idle?
questions.explanation: A cold start happens when the platform must spin up a new execution environment before running your code.

questions.prompt: Match each storage type to its description.
pairs: Flat, massive storage accessed as whole files
Raw disks attached to one machine
A shared filesystem many machines use at once
questions.explanation: Object, block, and file storage differ in structure and how many machines can use them.

questions.prompt: A service offers 99.9% availability. Using a 365-day year (8,760 hours), how many hours of downtime per year does that allow, to two decimal places?
questions.explanation: 0.1% of 8,760 hours is 8.76 hours of allowed downtime per year.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly contrasts durability and availability?
choices: Durability is whether data survives; availability is whether you can reach it right now
Durability is whether you can reach data right now; availability is whether it survives
They are two names for the same measure
Durability only applies to block storage
questions.answer: Durability is whether data survives; availability is whether you can reach it right now
questions.explanation: A service can have eleven nines of durability yet still be briefly unreachable.

questions.prompt: A CDN caches content on servers located close to users so it can be delivered with lower latency.
questions.explanation: Serving cached copies from nearby edge servers shortens the trip for the user.

questions.prompt: Which load-balancing algorithm sends each new request to the server that currently has the fewest active connections?
choices: Least connections
Round robin
Random
Sticky hashing
questions.explanation: Round robin hands out requests in turn regardless of load; least connections steers away from the busiest server.

questions.prompt: A web app has web servers and a database inside one VPC. Explain how public and private subnets should be used, and why.
rubric: Puts the web servers in a public subnet with an internet route
Puts the database in a private subnet with no internet route
Says the database is reachable only from inside the VPC (such as from the web servers)
Explains this limits exposure even if an attacker learns the database's address
questions.model: Place the web servers in a public subnet that has a route to the internet through a gateway, so users can reach them. Put the database in a private subnet with no internet route, reachable only from the web servers over the VPC's internal network, so even someone who learns its address has no path to it.
questions.explanation: Public subnets host what must be reachable; private subnets keep sensitive resources off the internet.

questions.prompt: What does using a managed database change for you?
choices: The provider handles tasks like backups and patching, while you still design schemas and queries
You no longer need to design a schema
You must handle all backups yourself
The database can only run on your own hardware
questions.answer: The provider handles tasks like backups and patching, while you still design schemas and queries
questions.explanation: Managed services take over operations work, not your application's data design.

questions.prompt: Match each IAM term to its meaning.
pairs: A bundle of permissions that can be assigned
A document stating what actions are allowed or denied
Granting only the access needed for the task
questions.explanation: Roles and policies express permissions, and least privilege is the principle for deciding how much to grant.

questions.prompt: In a publish/subscribe setup, every subscriber receives a copy of each message, rather than just one consumer getting it.
questions.explanation: A plain work queue delivers each message to one consumer, while pub/sub fans a copy out to all subscribers.

questions.prompt: Which is an example of horizontal scaling?
choices: Adding more server instances behind a load balancer
Moving to a single bigger server
Adding more RAM to one VM
Upgrading one VM's CPU
questions.answer: Adding more server instances behind a load balancer
questions.explanation: Horizontal scaling adds more machines; vertical scaling makes one machine bigger.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the charge for data leaving the provider's network that often surprises people on a cloud bill?
questions.explanation: Moving data in is usually free, but data transferred out (egress) is metered and billed.

questions.prompt: Running every server in one availability zone removes single points of failure.
questions.explanation: If that zone fails, everything fails; redundancy needs copies across separate availability zones.

questions.prompt: What is vendor lock-in?
choices: How difficult or costly it is to switch away from a provider because of dependence on its non-standard services
A legal contract that forbids changing providers
A discount for staying with one provider
A requirement that all providers' services be identical
questions.answer: How difficult or costly it is to switch away from a provider because of dependence on its non-standard services
questions.explanation: Lock-in is about the real cost of switching, and it exists on a spectrum.

questions.prompt: Which choices tend to reduce vendor lock-in?
choices: Using containers that run on any provider
Choosing a managed service built on an open-source engine
Favoring widely adopted, non-proprietary technologies
Building around a proprietary event system unique to one provider
Using a database flavor that exists only at one provider
answers: Using containers that run on any provider
Choosing a managed service built on an open-source engine
questions.explanation: Portable, standard technologies are easier to move; proprietary services tie the application to one vendor.

questions.prompt: More provider-managed convenience can mean more lock-in, so avoiding lock-in is not automatically the right choice.
questions.explanation: The course frames lock-in as a tradeoff: convenience from proprietary services can be worth the reduced portability.
